- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially after recent price spikes; reduce forecast by 2–5% for the first 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >95), model fails to correct downward quickly; apply a “cool-down” bias: subtract 1–3% per day for the next 5–10 days.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: forecasts often overshoot the 30-day average; cap forecast at 1.5–2x the 30-day moving average for the first 10 days.
- Sentiment history is flat (all 0.00) — no corrective signal — so do not adjust for sentiment; treat as neutral market.
- If true outcome shows a sharp drop after a peak, model tends to underestimate the drop; add a 1–2% downward adjustment for the 3–5 days following the peak.
- Model underestimates the “tail” of the 30-day horizon (last 5–7 days) — especially after a dip — so add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for the final 5 days if true outcome shows recovery.
